title: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon: the sefiros that are not in the Essence and cannot be taken out of it
overview:
The series begins here. Its introduction calls *Shaar HaYichud* a book in two parts: what *hisbonenus* is (not meditation but *iyun*, detailed analytical study, as a doctor must know every particular), and, from chapter 10, what to contemplate: every world and every *sefira* in particulars.

The chapter starts at the top, with the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, in three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*. The texts say there are no ten *sefiros* there, and they say He engraved letters there, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*. The answer is the kind man. His kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches; yet a kindness that will not do shoes is no kindness at all, "just a bureaucracy", and the pants he never gave are in it too. So with the *Aibershter*: take out one *sefira* and you are a *kofer*; and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich, the actual car, comes from there. In the soul the same three levels run from powers that *mamash* do not exist, through powers ready to come out, to the estimate of one grab for the vodka bottle; and to reach the physical it takes a *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: From here on: every world, every sefira, in particulars
sections.summary: The first part of the book taught that *hisbonenus* is detailed study; from chapter 10 the book begins the subject itself, the four worlds and their *sefiros* down to particulars of particulars, and how each world's *Keser* joins it to the one above.

phrases.en: (10) Now, we have to understand *derech prat* (in the particular way) all four worlds of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*:

phrases.he: דהיינו בכל פרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאבי''ע
phrases.en: that is, in all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*,

phrases.he: בכל פרטיהן,
phrases.en: in all their particulars;

phrases.he: גם בכל ספירה שמתחלקת לפרטי פרטיות

blocks.text:
*Shaar HaYichud*, the Gate of Unification of the *Mitteler Rebbe*, the second Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi DovBer, is called the Key to Kabbala and *Chassidus*, and also *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*, the book of contemplation. It has two parts. The first explains what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is; the second, starting in chapter 10, explains what to do the contemplation on.

The first part is a direct sequel to another book of the *Mitteler Rebbe*, *Kuntres HaHispaalus*, on how to awaken the G-dly emotions, love and fear of G-d. There he explains that there is no real *hispaalus* (awakening of the emotions) unless it is preceded by proper *hisbonenus*.

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* is not what most people think. It is not meditation, which is based on concentration. It is a synonym for what the Talmud calls *iyun*: deep, repetitive, analytical study, the kind one would have to do on any subject. You go over the subject again and again, and each time you look at it in a slightly new way, and every time you go over it you discover new angles in it.

blocks.title: The doctor and the engineer
blocks.text: To become an adept at any subject one has to study it in detail. Most of us know in general what medicine is about, or engineering, or chemistry, and that does not make us a doctor or an engineer or a chemist. A doctor has to know the particulars: all the parts of the human body, all the different medicines and all the different maladies, and which medicine works for which malady. The same with any other subject. And the deeper the subject, the more one has to study it, and the more detail, and the more kinds of explanation, one needs to become an adept at it.

blocks.text: Kabbala and *Chassidus*, whose subject is G-dliness, are therefore the deepest study there is and need the most study. It is not possible to go to a cave someplace, meditate on G-dliness and expect to become an adept at G-dliness. The only way is through studying the Kabbala that G-d gave us on Mount Sinai. The subject is totally unknowable by the human mind and cannot be researched and arrived at by human effort. But G-d Himself could give it: when He gave Moses the Torah, with the oral Torah, on Mount Sinai, He gave him all its explanations, the kabbalistic explanations of G-dliness among them.

blocks.text: The *hisbonenus*, the deep analytical study, has to go together with concentration, both during the study and afterwards: during the study one must concentrate, or one gets no benefit from it, and after studying the subject one has to think about it. What one learns is the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds): how the worlds come down from the infinite light, through creation something from nothing, through the four universes of emanation, creation, formation and action, all the way down to our physical universe. One has to know all its details, and then contemplate what one has learned.

blocks.text: That is a synopsis of the first part of the book: *hisbonenus* is not meditative concentration, focusing the mind on a single thing, but a deep analytical study of all the details of the chain of worlds from the infinite light down to ours. So the course begins at chapter 10, where the second part begins and the book starts to explain what the *hisbonenus* will be on. (He stops, "I'm sorry", and says it again more exactly.)

blocks.text: First, the general framework of the Kabbala: how the four worlds come down from the infinite light. Before the worlds came into being, the entire space where they are now was full of the absolutely infinite light of G-dliness. To create a world there had to be a space for it, so G-d, so to speak, removed the light from a certain place, in a circle, or rather like a sphere, leaving a place where the world could be created. Into that sphere He emanated a very thin line of light, finite in comparison to the infinite light before, and from it, through more and more *tzimtzumim* (lessenings of the light), He finally brought it down to the very finite world we live in.

blocks.text: To recap: the removal of the light from the space is the first *tzimtzum*. What was left over is a *reshimu*, an impression of the light, and from it He drew out the thin, finite line of light from which the worlds were created. In each world there is less and less light: more in the world of emanation, less going down through creation, formation and action, and at the end of the world of action is the world of the *kelipos* (the shells), where we are: the externalities, sometimes called the evil influences. That is why in this world there is an actual possibility of evil, and of its seeming as if there is no G-d.

blocks.text: "Now, chapter 10." Now that he has told us that *hisbonenus* has to be done *derech prat*, he is going to explain in the *derech prat*. **all the particulars of the ten *sefiros***: this is what he is going to explain, everything.

He is going to explain all the particulars, and **every *sefira*, which divides into particulars of particulars**: *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*, five levels. That means any five levels. When you finish this thing you should be able to figure it out; and really *v'chahai gavna*, "and the like", means even six levels.

phrases.he: וענין יחודם והתכללותם
phrases.en: And the matter of their unification and their inclusion

phrases.he: בבחינת הכתר שבכל עולם,
phrases.en: in the *Keser* of each world,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הממוצע בין עולם העליון לתחתון הימנו
phrases.en: which is the intermediary between the upper world and the one below it,

phrases.he: כידוע הכלל דרך קיצור
phrases.en: as the rule is known, in short:

phrases.he: שמבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון, עד רום המעלות.
phrases.en: the *Malchus* of the upper becomes the *Keser* of the lower, up to the highest of levels.

blocks.text: How everything is included in the *Keser* of each world, the intermediary between a world and the one below it, by the known rule that the *Malchus* of the upper becomes the *Keser* of the lower: "that's what is going to be explained in chapter 10 through the end of the book."

sections.title: First the Source of everything: the Essence before the tzimtzum, in three levels
sections.summary: Before the worlds, one has to contemplate *Mekora d'Kula*, the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and that too in particulars. In general it divides into three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, each of ten *sefiros*, all still inside the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: אך הנה מתחלה
phrases.en: However, first of all

phrases.he: יש לכל מתבונן להתבונן במקור הראשון
phrases.en: every contemplator has to contemplate the first source,

phrases.he: הנקרא מקורא דקולא
phrases.en: called *Mekora d'Kula*, the source of everything,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: which is the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*

phrases.he: שלפני הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: before the *tzimtzum*, which is called the *makom panui* (the empty place), mentioned above.

blocks.text: Now that we are getting started, first of all we have to get started with a certain thing: **the first source, … called *Mekora d'Kula*, the source of everything**. It is the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum*, the *tzimtzum* that is called the *makom panui*.

phrases.he: גם שם דרך פרט דוקא
phrases.en: There too, *davka* (specifically) in the particular way.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא מאריך באחד,
phrases.en: This is what is called *ma'arich b'echad* (lengthening the word *Echad*),

phrases.he: באחדות הפשוטה דוקא
phrases.en: *davka* in the simple oneness.

blocks.text: Over there too we are going to look *derech prat*. That is the inner meaning of *ma'arich b'echad*, drawing out the word *Echad* in "*Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad*": that one looks at length into **the simple oneness**.

phrases.he: ונחלק לג' מדריגות דרך כלל
phrases.en: And it divides into three levels, in general,

phrases.he: ובכל א' כלול מי׳ ספירות
phrases.en: and each one includes ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: והוא יחיד ואחד וקדמון,
phrases.en: These are *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*;

phrases.he: והכל בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and all of it is the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, before the first *tzimtzum* mentioned above.

blocks.text:
**in general** we divide it into three levels. Really, of course, it divides into many more levels, because these three are only the levels of the *pnimiyus ha'or* (the inner aspect of the light). He is not even talking about the *Maor* (the source of the light) here. The *pnimiyus ha'or* divides into three levels, and then there is the *hispashtus ha'or* (the spreading forth of the light). He is talking about the *etzem ha'or*, the light itself, and, as we were just saying before, there are more levels; but in general we are talking about the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the Essence of the infinite light) here. **each one includes ten *sefiros***.

The three levels are *Yachid* (singular), *Echad* (one) and *Kadmon* (preceding). And all this is still inside the *Atzmus*.

sections.title: Yachid: no ten sefiros, and yet ten sefiros included
sections.summary: *Yachid* is *mamash* alone, above even a unification, so in the Essence one cannot speak of ten *sefiros*. Yet just as speech shows a will and a brain behind it, the Essence includes ten *sefiros*: wise, but not with a wisdom you could separate out. The *middos* come from Him; they do not describe Him.

phrases.he: בחינת יחיד משמעו לבדו ממש
phrases.en: *Yachid* means *mamash* (actually, literally) alone,

phrases.he: והוא למעלה מהתאחדות נפרדים
phrases.en: which is above a unification of separate things,

phrases.he: שנקרא אחד כידוע
phrases.en: which is called *Echad*, as is known.

phrases.he: ולפי זה בבחינת העצמות ממש
phrases.en: So in the Essence itself

phrases.he: לא יתכן לומר עדיין ענין עשר ספירות כלל
phrases.en: one cannot yet speak of ten *sefiros* at all.

phrases.he: וכמו מלכות דאין סוף,
phrases.en: As with *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*:

phrases.he: שממילא מובן שקדם לזה בחינת כתר וחכמה כו'
phrases.en: from it one understands by itself that *Keser* and *chachma* came before it.

blocks.title: Speech means a will and a brain
blocks.text: He reads that **one cannot yet speak of ten *sefiros* at all**, and then the comparison: *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, which by itself shows that *Keser* and *chachma* came before it. *Malchus* means speech. If you see speech somewhere, there has to be a *ratzon* (will) and a brain. You cannot have speech without a will and a brain.

phrases.he: ובאמת גם בבחינת העצמות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: And in truth, even the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*

phrases.he: שנקרא לבדו
phrases.en: which is called *Levado* (Alone)

phrases.he: כלול בעצמו י׳ ספירות
phrases.en: includes in itself ten *sefiros*;

phrases.he: אך שנקרא חכים לא בחכמה ידיעא כידוע,
phrases.en: only it is called "wise, but not with a known wisdom", as is known,

phrases.he: עד ולאו מכל אלין מדות כלל.
phrases.en: up to "and not of any of these attributes at all."

blocks.text: **includes in itself ten *sefiros***. And by the way, this level that is called *Levado*: in *Emek HaMelech* (a Kabbalistic work) he calls the *Maor* and the *Levad* levels of *Yachid*. In other words, here he is talking about the most external level of *Yachid*, which is the most inward level of the *Or Ein Sof*. So even the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* includes in itself ten *sefiros*.

**"wise, but not with a known wisdom"** means: not with a discernible *chachma* (wisdom). It can be explained in different ways too, but the main explanation is that He is wise, but not with a wisdom that can be separated out so that you can know: this is the wisdom. And then **"and not of any of these attributes at all"**: it is not only that He is not wise with a known wisdom; He really is not of these *middos* (attributes) at all. Just the opposite: the *middos* come from Him. Not that they describe Him in any way.

sections.title: His light as He is, and yet letters engraved: a Keser and a Malchus in the Essence
sections.summary: The *Or Ein Sof* is simple like the Essence, "He and His Name", the *tehiru ila'a*, a revelation of Him to Himself, where even "unity" does not fit. The names wise and kind are only from what He would be after the *tzimtzum*; and yet the Zohar's *glif glifu* puts a head and an end, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*, inside the Essence: "*Ana Emloch*", which the souls of Israel precede.

phrases.he: והענין הוא
phrases.en: The matter is this:

phrases.he: דבאמת כמו שעצמות האין סוף הוא אור פשוט בתכלית הפשיטות,
phrases.en: in truth, just as the Essence of the *Ein Sof* is a simple light, utterly simple,

phrases.he: כך ממש בחינת אורו וזיוו הנקרא אור אין סוף
phrases.en: so *mamash* is His light and radiance, called the *Or Ein Sof*:

phrases.he: דהיינו הוא ושמו בלבד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is, only He and His Name, as mentioned above.

blocks.text: First he is talking about the *Maor*, the Essence, which is **a simple light, utterly simple**; and **so *mamash* is His light and radiance** (*mamash*: actually, literally): **only He and His Name**. The word *bilvad* (only) here is a total hint; he is not really explaining it here. The simple meaning is that there is only Him and His Name: there is no other level, that is all there is. But really it is within the matter of *Levado*. So "Him and His Name" means: the *Atzmus Ein Sof* is "He", and the *Or Ein Sof* is "His Name".

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא טהירו עילאה
phrases.en: This is what is called *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity),

phrases.he: שזהו ענין ובחינת התגלות אור עצמותו
phrases.en: which is the revelation of the light of His Essence

phrases.he: כמו שהוא דוקא
phrases.en: *davka* exactly as it is.

blocks.text: This whole matter of the *tehiru ila'a* is everything before the *tzimtzum*. *Kadmon* too is still *tehiru ila'a*, not only *Yachid*.

**the revelation of the light of His Essence *davka* exactly as it is** (*davka*: specifically, precisely): the actual revelation, exactly as He is. It is explained in another place that the *etzem Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is really a revelation to Himself. It is still not the revelation that is going to go out to others. It is just to Himself, not to anybody else. It is *mamash* to nobody.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא יחיד,
phrases.en: This is what is called *Yachid*:

phrases.he: שאין עוד מלבדו
phrases.en: there is no more besides Him

phrases.he: לומר בו לשון התאחדות או לשון יחוד
phrases.en: to speak of Him in terms of unification, or of unity.

phrases.he: וזהו אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י' כו'.
phrases.en: And this is "You are One, and not in a count": [the count of] ten.

blocks.text: **there is no more besides Him**, *ein od milvado*. But remember that this *ein od milvado* is really its most external part: the actual *gilui* (revelation) of it, which can almost be called its *hispashtus* (spreading forth). **to speak of Him in terms of unification, or of unity**: you really cannot even call it a unification or a unity, because it does not apply to it. Even to call it *Yachid* is wrong, since he just said *yichud*, and *Yachid* is a word of *yichud*, unity.

It says, *Ant hu chad v'lo b'chushban*, and the commentary on it is "ten". Not with what count? He says: You are one, and not with a count, not with a mathematics. Which mathematics? Ten: that is the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אך מה שאמרו חכים ולא בחכמה ידיעא כו'
phrases.en: But what they said, "wise, but not with a known wisdom",

phrases.he: שיש על כל פנים חלוקי מדריגות,
phrases.en: that there are at any rate distinctions of levels,

phrases.he: חכים ומבין חסדן ורחמן כו'
phrases.en: wise and understanding, kind and merciful,

phrases.he: הכל לא מצד עצמותו,
phrases.en: all this is not from the side of His Essence,

phrases.he: רק מצד מה ששיער בעצמו בכח
phrases.en: only from what He estimated in Himself, in potential,

phrases.he: מה שעתיד להיות בפועל אחר הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: of what would be in actuality after the first *tzimtzum* mentioned above.

blocks.question: If there are levels at all, why do they say He is wise but not with a known wisdom? And if there is no chachma there, how can He be called wise?
blocks.text: This thing we are calling "wise" does not really describe Him. It is only that since He made people with *chachma* and *bina*, you have to say that He is a *chacham* (a wise man). But what do you mean, you have to say He is wise? We just said there is no *chachma*.

Usually, when you say "this guy has no *chachma*", it means he is stupid. When we say of the *Aibershter* (the One Above) that there is no *chachma* there, it does not mean a lack of *chachma*. It means **not with a known wisdom**: not like your *chachma*. It is so far beyond *chachma* that you cannot say *chachma* there.

And it is not only that you cannot say *chachma* there: the whole matter of *chachma* comes from Him. Not only does *chachma* not define Him; He defines the *chachma*, and the *chachma* gets everything from Him, not the other way round. By a *chacham*, what defines him is the fact that he is a *chacham*.

That is one thing. Another: the real matter of *chachma*, as we learned before, is that *chachma* also means stupidity. It is the same as *taanug* (delight). *Taanug* does not mean pleasure; it means the power to have pleasure or the opposite. The ability to feel pain comes from the *Keser*, from *pnimiyus haKeser*, of *Atik*, the same as the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to be stupid also comes from Him. And when you say "wise, but not with a known wisdom", you will have to say too that He is stupid, not with a known stupidity: not a stupidity like you think. The *Aibershter*'s is a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

sensitivity.reason: Says that G-d is "stupid, not with a known stupidity"; some readers would take the wording as irreverent, like the film joke after it.
sensitivity.publishable: That is one thing. Another: the real matter of *chachma*, as we learned before, is that *chachma* also includes its opposite. It is the same as *taanug* (delight). *Taanug* does not mean pleasure; it means the power to have pleasure or the opposite. The ability to feel pain comes from the *Keser*, from *pnimiyus haKeser*, of *Atik*, the same as the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to lack wisdom also comes from Him. And when you say "wise, but not with a known wisdom", you will have to say too that the opposite of wisdom is in Him, not as you think it: the *Aibershter*'s is a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

blocks.text: In other words, nobody can beat the *Aibershter*. If you are going to play a stupid game, the *Aibershter* would win. "You know, like they had a movie, *Dumb and Dumber*. If there was a contest who could be the dumbest of them all, the *Aibershter* would win."

sensitivity.reason: A joke that G-d would win a contest for the dumbest, by way of a film comedy; some readers would take it as irreverent.

blocks.text: And this is one of the things we are talking about with "the place": there has to be a place for stupidity. Think about it: otherwise you could not have a stupid person. There has to be a place for his stupidity. So in the same way, He gives existence to the *chachma*, so that *chachma* means both things, both lines.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקדש מלך בלשון האריז''ל עצמו ומבואר במקום אחר באריכות)
phrases.en: (As is written in *Mikdash Melech*, in the words of the Arizal himself, and explained elsewhere at length.)

phrases.he: וזהו ענין כללות המאמר הראשון בזוהר,
phrases.en: And this is the general meaning of the first saying of the *Zohar*:

phrases.he: בריש הורמנא דמלכא גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: "At the head of the King's authority, He engraved an engraving in the *tehiru ila'a*."

phrases.he: פירוש בעצמות גלוי אורו הפשוט הנזכר לעיל שנקרא טהירו עילאה,
phrases.en: That is: in the Essence of the revelation of His simple light mentioned above, called *tehiru ila'a*,

phrases.he: גליף גליפו שהוא ענין חקיקת אותיות
phrases.en: "He engraved an engraving", which is the engraving of letters.

blocks.text:
This is explained in *Mikdash Melech* (a commentary on the Zohar); this little blurb here is a reference, a footnote.

Then the first saying of the *Zohar*: **"He engraved an engraving", which is the engraving of letters**. He engraved letters. Later on we will learn that there is the *ratzon hapashut* (the simple will), and within the *ratzon hapashut* there is the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will); that is the engraving of letters.

phrases.he: ובריש הורמנא,
phrases.en: And "at the head of the authority":

phrases.he: שזה כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט,
phrases.en: that is when it arose in His simple will,

phrases.he: הוא בחינת כתר,
phrases.en: which is *Keser*;

phrases.he: ובחינת האותיות שחקק
phrases.en: and the letters that He engraved

phrases.he: הוא בחינת המלכות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: are the *Malchus* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: ואם כן יש ראש וסוף,
phrases.en: If so, there is a head and an end,

phrases.he: כתר ומלכות, גם בבחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: *Keser* and *Malchus*, even in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*.

blocks.text: **when it arose in His simple will**: that He wants a certain thing. So if you are telling me it is like this, **there is a head and an end, *Keser* and *Malchus***, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*. Not only that: you have to say there is a *chachma*, because how did He figure out how to make letters? "A dog can have a *ratzon*, and he can't write it." And you have to say there is a *bina*, because to divide into letters you have to have *bina*. And presumably, if there is *bina* there are *middos*.

phrases.he: וביאורו
phrases.en: And the explanation:

phrases.he: שעלה במחשבה ורצון הפשוט אנא אמלוך
phrases.en: it arose in the thought and the simple will, "*Ana Emloch*" (I shall rule);

phrases.he: והכל בעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: and all this is still within His Essence,

phrases.he: קודם ענין מה ששיער בעצמו בכח דוקא
phrases.en: before what He estimated in Himself, *davka* in potential,

phrases.he: כל מה שיהיה לו רצון למלוכה בגלוי,
phrases.en: of everything by which He would have a will for kingship in the open,

phrases.he: והוא אחר הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: which is after the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui*.

blocks.question: You just told us there is no Keser and Malchus there; now you are saying there is?
blocks.text: **And the explanation**: what is going on here? Before this he already did it several times: he said there is and there isn't. The explanation is that it **arose in the thought and the simple will, "*Ana Emloch*"**.

blocks.title: With whom did He consult? The Jews before "I shall rule"
blocks.text: "Over here there's a little thing I always stick in": *b'mi nimlach?* With whom did He consult? *B'nishmoseihem shel tzaddikim*, with the souls of the *tzaddikim* (the righteous). *Emloch* means "I will rule"; *nimlach* means "consult"; but basically it is the same word. So of *Ana Emloch* you can also ask whom He consulted, or through whom He became a king when He said "*Ana Emloch*". There had to be someone He was *nimlach* through. The souls of the *tzaddikim*, and "Your people are all *tzaddikim*": so the source of the Jews is really higher than the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought). The source of a Jew is in the *Ana Emloch*, and really higher than it, because "with whom did He consult?" means that they gave existence to the *Ana Emloch*. They preceded even the *Ana Emloch*. The Jews go all the way up.

**all this is still within His Essence**, before He actually figured it out. This is the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), and the *glif glifu* also has levels: a *glif glifu* in *Yachid*, one in *Echad* and one in *Kadmon*. The *shiur* (estimation) is in *Kadmon*. Usually they say that the *glif glifu* is a *shiur*, but there is a *glif glifu* higher than the *shiur*, which is what he says here: this is before the *shiur*, it is in the simple will, and we have not even got to *Echad*; we are talking about *Yachid*. So in *Yachid* itself there is a *glif glifu*, and the actual decision for the Jew is in *Yachid*.

Not only that: he also told you that the *Or Ein Sof* of *Yachid* is the revelation of the *Atzmus* exactly as it is. Since there is a *glif glifu* in the *Or Ein Sof*, it really came from the *Atzmus*. Really it is the *Aibershter* who wants the Jew. If He did not, the Jew could not exist, because He is the place of everything: the light could not do something the *Aibershter* would not give a place for. "You know what I'm talking about?" So there is a revelation; and really it goes even higher than this, although the text does not talk about it, since it speaks only of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*.

**which is after the *tzimtzum***: the *shiur* is what will be after the *tzimtzum*. So what exactly is going on here? From one side we are saying it is a perfect unity that has no parts, and then we are talking about parts.

sections.title: The kind man: a hiyuli desire for kindness that holds every particular
sections.summary: A kind person's kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches, yet a kindness that lacks one of them is no kindness at all, and every particular, even pants he never gave, comes out of it. So too the ten *sefiros* are in the Essence: not as parts, and not removable, and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich comes from there.

phrases.he: והדמיון בזה ידוע
phrases.en: The comparison for this is known

phrases.he: מכחות הנפש בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה
phrases.en: from the powers of the soul, as they are revealed from the will down to the deed:

phrases.he: שישנם כולם בפרט
phrases.en: they are all there, in particular,

phrases.he: בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה
phrases.en: hidden in the light of the soul's essence, called *yechida*.

blocks.text: **they are all there, in particular**: the various powers. The *yechida* (the essence of the soul) is a unitary thing and is not made up of powers, but nonetheless you have to say that the powers are there.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא
phrases.en: For example,

phrases.he: כאשר האדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להטיב בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: when a person has a *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) and goodness, to do good in a particular thing,

phrases.he: שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זאת דחפץ חסד וטוב
phrases.en: it comes from his having this attribute of desiring kindness and goodness

phrases.he: בבחינת עצמות נפשו, הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: in the essence of his soul, called *yechida*.

phrases.he: על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגלוי מן העלמו
phrases.en: That is why this desire for kindness comes into the open out of its hiddenness.

blocks.text: It means that he is a kind person himself: the himself is kind. But you say, "Wait a minute, how can you say that the himself is kind? The himself is just the himself. It's not made up of *middos*." Yes, it is not made up of *middos*. But on the other hand, if he is kind, it is not that he is just him plus different kinds of add-ons. He himself is kind. So there has to be a kindness there; and even though it is not a separate, individual thing, you still have to say there is a particular like that there.

blocks.title: The schnorrers' recommendation
blocks.text:
**That is why this desire for kindness comes into the open**: he is kind, and you can see this by the *schnorrers* (beggars). The *schnorrers* tell each other where to go. One *schnorrer* says: "Go to this one, he's a good guy, he'll help you." So you say, "How do you know he'll help me? What, do you know the future?" "I don't have to know the future. He's a good guy, that's why he'll help you." "How do you know he's a good guy? Did you see his goodness?" "No, I didn't see his goodness. But he helped me, and he helped Shloimy over here, and he helped Chaimy. So I figure that since he's helping everybody, he must be a good guy."

Not that he *has* a kindness: if you say he has a kindness, then maybe he lost his kindness today. Maybe he got hit on the head and the kindness kind of went away. "No, he's a good guy himself." That is what it means: he himself is a good guy. That is why the *chafetz chesed* comes out from its hiddenness, and that is why he helped me, and Shloimy, and Chaimy.

phrases.he: ומוכרח לומר בוודאי
phrases.en: So you have to say for sure

phrases.he: שחפץ חסד זה בעצמות נפשו
phrases.en: that this desire for kindness in the essence of his soul

phrases.he: הוא בבחינת כח היולי בעצמיות
phrases.en: is a *hiyuli* (raw, formless) power, in essence,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב
phrases.en: to include everything he will ever want of kindness and good,

phrases.he: בכל פרטי פרטי הענינים שיבקשו ממנו
phrases.en: in all the particulars of particulars that will be asked of him.

blocks.title: Shoes, coats, sandwiches, and pants
blocks.text: It is not a kindness like this. "Well, what did he do for you?" "I needed shoes and he gave me shoes." "Oh yeah? So what did he do for Chaimy?" "He needed a coat and he gave him a coat." "And what did he do for Shloimy?" "Shloimy was hungry and he gave him a sandwich." So you say: "So what kind of kindness does he have? He has a kindness for shoes, and a kindness for coats, and a kindness for sandwiches. But I need pants. Do you know anybody he gave pants to?" "Well, I don't know anybody he gave pants to, but he has a kindness. If you go and tell him you need pants, he'll give you pants." How do you know? He never gave pants to anybody before. Why? Because we have to say that the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli*.

**to include everything he will ever want of kindness and good**, any kind of good thing, **in all the particulars of particulars that will be asked of him**. If you go and ask him for pants, it is included in the *hiyuli*.

On the next side, once the foundation example is finished (4:22), he sums up: in the essential, *hiyuli* desire for kindness are included all the particular things that people will ask of him. "I'm going to start from the third line here", and he reads the two lines again: shoes, sandwiches, whatever.

Not only that: if you say that one particular is missing, then it is not *chesed*. Really it is not made up of the particulars. You cannot say that the essential *chafetz chesed* of a person is made up of *ratzonos* (wills) to give sandwiches and to give shoes and to give clothing; that is not what defines it, because what it is, is *chesed*, a thing of kindness. However, take out one particular, and it is not *chesed* anymore.

That is what it says in *Pasach Eliyahu* (Elijah's opening prayer, in the *Tikkunei Zohar*): whoever separates one of these ten *sefiros* from its fellow, it is as if he separated You. The *Atzmus* is not made of the *sefiros*, but if you take out one *sefira*, if you say "I'm going to take out *chesed*", you have made a separation, and it is not the *Aibershter* anymore. He is a *kofer* (denier) in the whole *Aibershter*.

For instance, if you say "G-d is love", that means He is not *din* (judgement). Some people say G-d is unconditional love. No: if you say that, you are taking out the attribute of *din*, and the attribute of *din* says there are conditions.

sensitivity.reason: "G-d is love" and "unconditional love" are slogans associated with Christian preaching; the rejection can be read as aimed at another religion.
sensitivity.publishable: For instance, if one says G-d is only love, with no *din* (judgement), one has taken out the attribute of *din*, and the attribute of *din* says there are conditions.

blocks.text: The same as if they say: "This guy does everything, he'll do anything for you, but he won't give you shoes. If you're walking around without shoes, too bad." That is not kindness anymore. So even though He is not made out of the particulars of the ten *sefiros*, if you take out one *sefira* it is no longer the *Aibershter*: "as if he separated You".

phrases.he: ואם כן בהכרח
phrases.en: So you have to say

phrases.he: שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה שבגלוי,
phrases.en: that before this revealed will and desire of his arose,

phrases.he: להטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי,
phrases.en: to do his kindness in this particular thing,

phrases.he: היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי
phrases.en: it was included in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness,

phrases.he: ויצא מן ההיולי להתגלות בדבר פרטי זה
phrases.en: and it came out from the *hiyuli* to be revealed in this particular thing.

blocks.text: **So you have to say** that a *chesed* for pants was included. You see that a *chesed* for pants came out; if there was not a *chesed* for pants there, how could it come out? On the other hand, you cannot say that the essential *chafetz chesed* is made up of these different *chassadim* (kindnesses) for pants and coats and sandwiches. So from one side you have to say that the pants and coats and sandwiches are there.

And in the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) you *mamash* have to say it. In the *mashal* there is no actual sandwich in the *chesed*. You can say there is a *chesed* for sandwiches: in the *hiyuli* desire for kindness of a kind person there is included a *chesed* for sandwiches. But the sandwich does not come out of the *chafetz chesed*; unless he is a rich guy he will not be able to just keep giving out sandwiches. The sandwiches are external. In the *nimshal*, the actual sandwich comes from there.

"And this is the thing that people tend to fail to understand." They see it as more and more abstract. In a way it is like the *chafetz chesed* in the *mashal*: you cannot say there is an actual *chafetz chesed* of a sandwich. Never mind that there is a sandwich there; even to say there is a *chesed* for sandwiches there is ridiculous, "it's stupid". It is not a *chesed* for sandwiches; it is a *chesed*. But by the *Aibershter* it is the same thing.

blocks.title: Thanking Him for an idea of a sandwich
blocks.text:
You cannot say the *Aibershter* has sandwiches up there. So you say: "Wait a minute. I ate a sandwich, and you told me to *bentsh* (say the blessing after the meal) because the *Aibershter* gave me the sandwich. So if He didn't have this physical sandwich, why should I thank Him? Let me thank whoever gave me the physical sandwich. What, He had an idea for a sandwich? For what? I don't care about the idea for a sandwich. I care about the actual sandwich that filled up my stomach. That's what I'm thanking Him for, not for an idea of a sandwich."

And you have to make a blessing before you eat the sandwich and after. Why? Because the actual sandwich came from there: that means the *Aibershter* has sandwiches. In a way it is a stupid thing to say; but in a way it is a stupid thing to say the opposite too. If He did not have the sandwiches, where do they come from?

So you have to say that the essential *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli* power that includes all the particular things they will ask of him. (He reads the line again.) This *chafetz chesed* for sandwiches had to be included in the *hiyuli* desire for kindness. In fact you have to say it to the point that if the *chafetz chesed* for sandwiches was not included in the *hiyuli* desire for kindness, the *hiyuli* desire for kindness is totally not a *chafetz chesed*. Take the particular out, and there is no *chesed*. What does that mean?

blocks.title: The foundation that only gives shoes
blocks.text: There are certain foundations that give shoes; that is what they do. You can go to the foundation and drop dead on the floor from starvation, and they will not give you a sandwich. Why? Because their charter is to give shoes. Originally it might have started from some kind guy who, if you had got to him, would have given you a sandwich too; but he made up a foundation, and now the foundation gives shoes. It doesn't give sandwiches. So is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

sensitivity.reason: Charitable foundations are pictured as letting a man starve on their floor because of their charter.
sensitivity.publishable: Picture a foundation whose charter is to give shoes. A starving man comes in and asks for a sandwich, and they cannot give him one: their charter is shoes. It might have started from some kind man who would have given a sandwich too; but now it is a foundation, and it gives shoes. So is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

blocks.text: (After the tape is turned over.) It is not that you can't call it a *chafetz chesed* anymore because it does not take care of anything; it does take care of shoes. But not because of goodness. It is not a goodness. Even though it originated with goodness, now it is just a bureaucracy.

sensitivity.publishable: A kindness that has become bound by a charter does not give because of goodness any more, even though it originated with goodness.

blocks.title: Communism, a kindness of Tohu
blocks.text: "Some of the worst, terriblest things in the world came out of goodness, actually, like communism." You might say that Marx and Engels were slightly misguided, but their original idea was that everybody has certain needs that should be fulfilled. But then it got separated. That is the whole matter of *olam haTohu* (the world of Chaos): the original thing got separated from the *Atzmus*. So it is not a *chesed* anymore; it is a *chesed* of *Tohu*. They will give shoes to somebody, and yet somebody can *mamash* starve to death and they will not help him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

sensitivity.reason: Names communism, and Marx and Engels, among the worst things in the world.
sensitivity.publishable: Some of the worst things in the world came out of goodness: the original idea was that every person's needs should be met, and then it got separated. That is the whole matter of *olam haTohu* (the world of Chaos): the original thing got separated from the *Atzmus*. So it is not a *chesed* anymore; it is a *chesed* of *Tohu*. It will give shoes to somebody, and somebody else can *mamash* starve to death and it will not help him.

blocks.text: In a real *chesed*, if you say he is a really kind person, it is not like the foundation. There you cannot say, "These are kind people, go to them and they'll help you." You say: "But I don't need shoes, I got shoes. I need a coat." "Well, sorry, we don't give coats." So it is not a *chesed* anymore; it is just a bureaucracy. So not only do you have to say that the particular is there; if the particular was not there, the whole *chesed* is not there. If this guy will not give sandwiches, or will not give shoes, if he has all kinds of kindnesses but will not give you a sandwich, then he is not a kind guy. Whatever the reason he is doing it, it is not kindness; it is some other reason. So you have to say that this particular was included in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness, and came out of it.

blocks.text: And you have to say the same of the *Aibershter*. From one side He is above anything. From the other side you have to say that the *Aibershter* has sandwiches. If He doesn't have sandwiches, how can you say He is the *Aibershter*? If He is missing one sandwich, He is not the *Aibershter*.

blocks.text: "And not only kosher sandwiches. He's got *treif* (non-kosher) sandwiches."

blocks.title: "He ain't got no money"
blocks.text: As it says, "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold." It is translated to mean *chesed* and *gevura*, but really it means it literally. In *Shemoneh Esrei* (the eighteen blessings of the daily prayer) we ask Him, "Give me money." They say: "What are you going to Him for money for? He ain't got no money." So he says: "It doesn't mean He ain't got no money. It means that what He's got is way past money. It doesn't mean He's poor. If He wants, He can give you money. *Mamash* money."

phrases.he: ואנו רואים שיש בחפץ חסד זה
phrases.en: And we see that in this desire for kindness there is

phrases.he: שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה ודבור ומעשה
phrases.en: intellect and wisdom, and *middos*, and thought, speech and action.

phrases.he: אם כן ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו,
phrases.en: If so, certainly in the source of this desire for kindness, in its hiddenness,

phrases.he: כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי,
phrases.en: when it was included in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness,

phrases.he: גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה שבו
phrases.en: there was also the division of intellect, *middos*, thought, speech and action in it.

blocks.title: The drunk who says his family is starving
blocks.text: When the *chafetz chesed* of the essence comes into actuality, we see that there is a *sechel* (intellect) in it: when the person comes, you have to figure out exactly how to do this *chesed*. For instance, you think: "Wait a minute. This guy is coming and telling me his family is starving, but I know this guy's a drunk. If I give him money he'll spend it on liquor and come home and beat up his family, so I'm actually going to make it worse for them by giving him money. So what am I going to do? I'm going to send a bunch of food over to his wife, not to him. I'm going to actually bring the food over there." That shows there has to be a *sechel*.

sensitivity.reason: The example is a drunk who beats his family.
sensitivity.publishable: When the *chafetz chesed* of the essence comes into actuality, we see that there is a *sechel* (intellect) in it: when the person comes, you have to figure out exactly how to do this *chesed*. Sometimes money given to the man asking will not reach the family that needs it, so you send the food to the family yourself. That shows there has to be a *sechel*.

blocks.text: Then, to do the *chesed*, the man has to feel: there are *middos*. He has to feel a *chesed* and a pity in his heart. Then there is a *machshava* (thought): he thinks, "Okay, so let's do this." And a *dibur* (speech): when the guy asks him, he says, "Okay, I'll help you." And a *maaseh* (action). So it means there are ten *sefiros*: *sechel* is *chachma*, then all the *middos*, and thought, speech and action are *Malchus*.
**there was also the division**: otherwise, how could it come out like that? The revealed *chesed* has ten *sefiros*, so the hidden *chesed* also had to have ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי,
phrases.en: But in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness,

phrases.he: כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: as it is before it has come into a particular thing,

phrases.he: הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות כו',
phrases.en: even though certainly there too there is a division of intellect and *middos*,

phrases.he: מכל מקום כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית
phrases.en: still they are included and unified completely.

blocks.text: It is the same as the shoes and the sandwiches. Over there there were not really two different *chassadim*, and **unified** does not mean that they were connected together to build up a bigger *chesed*. It does not mean that. It means there really were not two separate things; it was only one thing. And the same with the ten *sefiros* of the essential *sefira*, of the essential *chafetz chesed*.

And later on he will say the same of the essential *chafetz chesed* in the actual *Atzmus Ein Sof*. In other words, the kindness within the *yechida* of a person is no more separate than the shoes and the sandwiches are separate, or than the ten *sefiros* of the *chafetz chesed* are separate. And in the same way the *chafetz chesed* itself is not separate from the other *sefiros*, and not really separate from the *Atzmus*.

sections.title: Every attribute alike, down to kingship: "I shall rule"
sections.summary: *Chesed* is only the example; every attribute, *netzach* with its strategy and its pep talk, down to *Malchus*, is made of ten, all one before it comes to a particular. He picked *chesed* and *Malchus* because the world comes from the desire for kindness and from "*Ana Emloch*": there is no king without a people.

phrases.he: וכמו כן במדה פרטית אחרת שבעצמיות,
phrases.en: And so too with any other particular attribute in the essence,

phrases.he: כמו מדת הגבורה והתפארת והנצח וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: like the attribute of *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach* and the like,

phrases.he: עד בחינת המלכות
phrases.en: down to *Malchus*,

phrases.he: שהוא מדת ההתנשאות
phrases.en: which is the attribute of *hisnasus* (rising above):

phrases.he: שכלול בודאי מי', רצון וחפץ למלוכה וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה כו'.
phrases.en: it is certainly made of ten: a will and desire to rule, and wisdom, and *middos*, and thought, and so on.

blocks.text: *Chafetz chesed* is one particular *sefira* that he gave the example on, but really every other attribute in the essence is like that, **like the attribute of *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach* and the like**. For instance, a guy who likes to win: it is because he has the attribute of *netzach* (victory) in his soul.

blocks.title: The football game
blocks.text: You can see that he likes to win all kinds of things, with all the different particulars. And to win he has to have a *sechel* and *middos*. You see it by a football game: "even though it's a stupid football game", there is a strategy to it.

blocks.title: It's all strategy
blocks.text: "When I talk to people, you know, everybody here is into football." They talk, and he has no idea what they are talking about, and after they talk for a while they look at him for his comment; everybody makes his comment. He says, "Yeah, you know, it's all strategy." And they say, "Yeah, right, that's right." It's all strategy.

What does "strategy" mean? That in the attribute of *netzach* there has to be a *sechel*. Then there have to be *middos*: you know how they have the pep talk before the game? He is trying to build up their *middos*. And there are thought, speech and action in the *netzach*.

Any of these attributes you can give a *mashal* on, but he gave the *mashal* on *chesed*; "and by the way, I think he picked *chesed* in particular because the world comes from *chafetz chesed*". And he goes **down to *Malchus***, which is also the attribute the world came out from, **the attribute of *hisnasus***. It too **is certainly made of ten**, like all the other *sefiros*: the will and desire to rule, which is the *Keser*; *chachma*; *middos*; and thought, speech and action, *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

phrases.he: אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: But before it comes to be revealed in a particular thing,

phrases.he: כמו למלוך על מדינה זו וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: like ruling over this country and the like,

phrases.he: כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית
phrases.en: they are included and unified completely

phrases.he: בבחינת מדת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית
phrases.en: in the essential, *hiyuli* attribute of kingship,

phrases.he: כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל
phrases.en: as in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness mentioned above.

blocks.text: Now he is going back to what he said before, the *Ana Emloch*, which is the *glif glifu*. That is why he came back *davka* to *Malchus* and not to the other *sefiros*. The *chafetz chesed* was the arousal from above that brought about having a world in the first place; but the actual thing of the world was *Ana Emloch*, *Malchus*, the *glif glifu*. The *glif glifu* is letters, and letters are *Malchus*. And it is also the matter of *hisnasus* over another person, which brings about the whole existence of another person: "there is no king without a people."

But **before it comes to be revealed in a particular thing, like ruling over this country**, there was the original attribute of kingship. The *hiyuli* for it existed before it actually happened. **they are included and unified completely in the essential, *hiyuli* attribute of kingship**: the same thing, as we said before.

sections.title: Not even "unified": the powers within the soul's essence, and where the particulars come from
sections.summary: Tape 004 picks up in mid-discussion (lines 48 to 64 are not recorded): the eye has the power to see every shape, even a sofa some guy in China has, and the will for *chesed* holds a will for every particular, or where would they come from? In the *nimshal* not only the power comes from there: the actual sofa, the actual car, the physical world itself.

phrases.he: וא"כ מובן ממילא
phrases.en: So it is understood by itself

phrases.he: שבחינת מדת העצמיות דכח''ב וחג''ת ונהי''ם ההיולים שבעצמיות הנפש,
phrases.en: that the essential, *hiyuli* attributes of *chachma*, *bina* and *daas*, *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*, in the soul's essence,

phrases.he: לא יתכן לומר גם לשון זה שמתאחדים וכלולים
phrases.en: cannot even be described this way, that they are unified and included

phrases.he: בעצמיות הנפש הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: in the soul's essence, called *yechida*,

phrases.he: מאחר שאינן נבדלים מן העצם כלל
phrases.en: since they are not separate from the essence at all.

phrases.he: כמו מדת חפץ חסד ההיולי הנזכר לעיל שמוטבע בטבעית ועצמיות
phrases.en: Like the *hiyuli* desire for kindness mentioned above, which is imprinted in the nature and essence [of the soul]:

phrases.he: הגם שהוא חלק אחד הנמשך מעצם הנפש ממש,
phrases.en: even though it is one part drawn from the very essence of the soul,

phrases.he: שלמעלה מהיות חפץ חסד בעצמיות,
phrases.en: which is above being a desire for kindness in essence,

phrases.he: שזהו ענין פרטי ממהותה העצמית הפשוטה בתכלית
phrases.en: since that is a particular matter of its utterly simple essential being,

phrases.he: מכל מקום אי אפשר לומר בו
phrases.en: still one cannot say of it

phrases.he: שמתאחד במדת נצוח ההיולית הנטוע בעצם הנפש,
phrases.en: that it is unified with the *hiyuli* attribute of winning, planted in the soul's essence,

phrases.he: מאחר שמיוחדים שניהם בעצמות ואינן נבדלים כלל וכלל מן העצם
phrases.en: since both are one in the essence and are not separate from the essence at all.

phrases.he: על דרך דוגמא כח התנועה שנכלל ממש בעצם החי
phrases.en: For example, the power of movement, which is *mamash* included in the living being itself

phrases.he: קודם שמניעו לגמרי, שאינו נבדל מן העצם כלל
phrases.en: before it moves it at all, where it is not separate from the essence at all.

phrases.he: אף על פי שבגלוי כח התנועה להניע דבר פרט,
phrases.en: Although when revealed, the power of movement, to move a particular thing,

phrases.he: יתחלק לכמה פרטי אופנים,
phrases.en: divides into many particular ways,

phrases.he: אי אפשר לומר שכל אופני פרטי התנועה כלולים ומתאחדים היו,
phrases.en: one cannot say that all the particular ways of movement were included and unified

phrases.he: כשהיה כח התנועה נכלל בעצם החי
phrases.en: when the power of movement was included in the living being itself,

phrases.he: מאחר שאז לא היה בסוג וגדר תנועה כלל, לא בכלל ולא בפרט כו'
phrases.en: since then it was not in the category or bounds of movement at all, neither in general nor in particular.

phrases.he: וכן בחינת גילוי התפשטות החיות להחיות כל הגוף
phrases.en: So too the revelation of the spreading of life, to enliven the whole body,

phrases.he: בעודנו כלול לגמרי בעצם רוח החיים
phrases.en: while it is still wholly included in the essence of the spirit of life:

phrases.he: הגם שבגלויו מתחלק לראיה ושמיעה לעין ואוזן וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: although when revealed it divides into sight and hearing, for the eye and the ear, and the like,

phrases.he: שבודאי גם טרם בואו להתגשם בעין ואוזן בפועל,
phrases.en: and certainly even before it comes to be embodied in the eye and the ear in actuality,

phrases.he: היה כלול בו חיות הראיה הרוחנית לעין בפני עצמו,
phrases.en: there was included in it the spiritual life of sight for the eye on its own,

phrases.he: וחיות השמיעה באוזן בפני עצמו
phrases.en: and the life of hearing in the ear on its own,

phrases.he: מכל מקום קודם שבאה עצם הנפש לכלל בחינת התפשטות החיות,
phrases.en: still, before the essence of the soul comes to the spreading of life,

phrases.he: גם שכלול בה, הרי זה כהתכללות כח התנועה בעצם החי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: though it is included in it, it is like the inclusion of the power of movement in the living being, mentioned above.

phrases.he: וכל מה שמוכן ועתיד לבוא לידי גלוי בפועל החיות עדיין,
phrases.en: Whatever is still ready and about to come into the revealed activity of life:

phrases.he: יתכן היחוד וההתכללות דראיה ושמיעה וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: there unification and inclusion of sight and hearing and the like can apply;

phrases.he: אבל כאשר כלול לגמרי בעצם הנפש
phrases.en: but when it is wholly included in the essence of the soul

phrases.he: והיה כלא יש במציאות התפשטות חיות כלל וכלל
phrases.en: and it is as if there were no spreading of life in existence at all,

phrases.he: מצד עצם הנפש שלמעלה הרבה מבחינת התפשטות,
phrases.en: from the side of the soul's essence, which is far above spreading forth,

phrases.he: רק שכולל בעצמות גם כן בחינת ההתפשטות,
phrases.en: only that in its essence it includes spreading forth too,

phrases.he: כעצם החי שכולל בעצמו כח התנועה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like the living being that includes the power of movement in itself, as mentioned above,

phrases.he: אם כן איך יתכן בחינת היחוד והתכללות דפרטי אור וחיות
phrases.en: then how can there be unification and inclusion of particulars of light and life,

phrases.he: רק מצד שעתיד ומוכן לצאת בהתפשטות חיות בהתחלקות פרטי חיות
phrases.en: except because it is about to, and ready to, come out in a spreading of life divided into particulars of life?

phrases.he: מזה מוכרח לומר
phrases.en: From this one must say

phrases.he: שיש כל פרטים הללו בהתפשטות הכלולה בעצם לגמרי,
phrases.en: that all these particulars are in the spreading forth that is wholly included in the essence;

phrases.he: שאם לא כן
phrases.en: for if not,

phrases.he: מאין נמצאו פרטים הללו בגלוי ההתפשטות
phrases.en: where would these particulars in the revealed spreading forth come from?

blocks.question: The eye has a hiyuli to see the sofa and the table, round shapes and square shapes. What about a sofa some guy has in China, which you never saw and are never going to see?
blocks.text: Yes: the eye has the power to see that too. It is not only that it would see it if it were exposed to it; the power to see that particular shape already exists in the eye, and therefore it exists in the soul. That means all the shapes exist in the soul. ("Okay, but that's really the power to see the shapes, not the actual sofa itself." "Right.")
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; the reading of the lines before it is not recorded, and the discussion leads straight into this line.

blocks.text: The same with the will for *chesed*. We said a will for a *chesed* of a sandwich and a will for a *chesed* of a shoe; that is not the actual shoe, only a will for a *chesed* to give shoes. That is in the *mashal*. In the *nimshal* the actual shoe is coming out from it, and the actual sofa, and all the actual emotions a person has: both the mental and the emotional, the whole of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* all the way, including the actual final physicality, is coming out from there. So when it says "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold", it does not mean just the ability to earn money. It means that the actual thing is coming out of there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; it leads into this line.

blocks.title: Where did my car come from?
blocks.text: **where would these particulars … come from?** Where did my car come from? If you say, "Well, you can't say there's an actual car in the *Aibershter*", that's right. From one side, that is what we said here: you cannot say that in the actual *chesed* there is a *chesed* to help somebody fix his car. On the other hand, if you do not say there is a *chesed* to help somebody fix his car, you broke the whole *chesed*; it is not a *chesed* anymore. So if you say that my car actually existed inside the *Aibershter*, it sounds kind of silly; the *Aibershter* is not made up of cars. On the other hand, if you say that my car did not exist in the *Aibershter*, then it is not the *Aibershter*. So where did the car come from? What, from another *Aibershter*? It came from somewhere.

If it is a car, you say, "Yeah, but it's physical." Yeah, right, and where did this physical come from? You want to tell me there is an *Aibershter*, and then there is the physical world? That, the *Rambam* says in *Moreh Nevuchim*, is the mistake the Greek philosophers made: they felt there is an *Aibershter* and there is also a physical world. Well, where did the physical world come from? You have to say it was also there.

And how can you say so, if there is nothing but the *Aibershter*? The same way you say that in the essential *chesed* there were all the particulars. So all the particulars are there. In the *mashal* that is the particular of just a *chesed* for a particular, not the actual sandwich; in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich came out from there, not just a will to give a sandwich, which was really something separate from Him. So you have to say: **where would these particulars in the revealed spreading forth come from?**

phrases.he: כמו האור וזיו שכלול בעצם השמש,
phrases.en: Like the light and radiance included in the body of the sun,

phrases.he: שיש בו בהעלם כל פרטי אופני זיו המתפשט
phrases.en: which has in it, hidden, all the particular kinds of the radiance that spreads out,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.
phrases.en: and the like. This is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: When the light was inside the sun it already had all the particulars. When you go outside and see the sunlight, you see the green and blue and yellow and whatever: it must already have been inside the sun. "So that's the end of this little section here": that was the general explanation of the whole thing. Now he is going to explain how it comes in three levels.

sections.title: Three levels drawn from the yechida: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon
sections.summary: *Yachid*: powers so wholly within the *yechida* that they *mamash* do not exist. *Echad*: powers ready to come out, like Avraham sitting at his tent with nobody yet come; here they are a unity of many abilities. *Kadmon*: the exact estimate of one act, complete even when something stops it, like the hand already set for the bottle that someone else grabs.

phrases.he: ונמצא ג' מדריגות זה אחר זה נמשך מעצמיות הנפש ממש,
phrases.en: So there are three levels, one after another, drawn *mamash* from the essence of the soul,

phrases.he: הנקרא בחינת יחידה
phrases.en: called *yechida*.

phrases.he: הא' י' כחות עצמיים והיוליים,
phrases.en: The first: ten essential, *hiyuli* powers,

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד העצמי והיולי וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: like the essential, *hiyuli* desire for kindness, and the like,

phrases.he: כלולים בה בתכלית,
phrases.en: wholly included in it,

phrases.he: כהתכללות כח התנועה בעצם החי
phrases.en: as the power of movement is included in the living being itself,

phrases.he: וכהתכללות התפשטות החיות בעצם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and as the spreading of life is included in the essence, as mentioned above.

phrases.he: ולא יתכן בהם לומר לשון התאחדות מדברים נבדלים יחד
phrases.en: One cannot speak of them as a unification of separate things together,

phrases.he: אחר שכלולים לגמרי בעצם,
phrases.en: since they are wholly included in the essence

phrases.he: והיה כלא היה במציאות כלל וכלל כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and are as if they did not exist at all, as mentioned above.

blocks.text: This is the matter of *Yachid*. **wholly included in it** means they *mamash* do not exist. It is like the power of movement in the living being: it is not just that they do not exist; the *yechida* is not even in the bounds and limits of them at all, not in that category. So **one cannot speak of them as a unification**: you cannot even say it is a unification. **as if they did not exist at all**: they *mamash* do not exist, totally. So that is *Yachid*.

phrases.he: והב' בחינת התפשטות י' כחות
phrases.en: The second: the spreading forth of ten powers

phrases.he: שמוכנים לבא בבחינת גלוי
phrases.en: that are ready to come into revelation,

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד העצמי ההיולי שבא לדבר חסד בדרך פרט
phrases.en: like the essential, *hiyuli* desire for kindness that comes to a particular act of kindness,

phrases.he: גם קודם שנמשך בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: even before it is drawn into actual deed,

phrases.he: רק כשעתיד ומוכן לצאת לדבר פרט
phrases.en: only when it is about to, and ready to, come out to a particular thing.

blocks.text: The second is *Echad*. It is already a thing of *hispashtus* (spreading forth): it is ready to come out in various ways, like *chesed*, or whichever of the ten *sefiros*.

blocks.title: Avraham sitting by the tent
blocks.text: **even before it is drawn into actual deed**: like when *Avraham Avinu* is sitting by the tent. He is already ready to have a *chesed* come out, but nothing is coming out, because nobody came yet. So there is a point where it is ready to come out to a particular, but you don't have a particular yet. It is just a thing, and that is *Echad*.

phrases.he: שם יתכן ענין האחדות מכמה פרטים שבו
phrases.en: There one can speak of the unity of the many particulars in it,

phrases.he: כמו שכל ומדות שבחפץ חסד זה
phrases.en: like the intellect and *middos* in this desire for kindness

phrases.he: הנמשך מהעלמות ההיולי הכללי כו'.
phrases.en: that is drawn from the hiddenness of the general *hiyuli*.

blocks.text: There you can say that it is made of various things, **like the intellect and *middos* in this desire for kindness**; and even there it is not *mamash* really a unification. **drawn from the hiddenness of the general *hiyuli***: if these powers came out of the essence, where they totally did not exist, you have to say there is a point where they started to have an ability to exist. It is not an actual existence, by the way; it is just an ability that it could exist. That is *Echad*, and there you can say that this ability is made up of a bunch of abilities, all unified together as the general *hispashtus* of the soul.

phrases.he: והג' כשנמשך ובא לאותו דבר פרט,
phrases.en: The third: when it is drawn and comes to that particular thing,

phrases.he: רק שעדיין לא בא מצד העדר ומניעה
phrases.en: only it has not yet come, because of an absence and a hindrance.

blocks.text: What does it mean? Not only when it does not come; really, even when it does come. When there is no absence and hindrance and it actually comes, when you are actually doing something, this third level is really connected to it. But it is *davka* when it does not come, because of an absence and a hindrance, that you can see it.

blocks.title: The bottle on the farbrengen table
blocks.text:
You are sitting at a *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering), there is a bottle of vodka on the table, your glass is empty, and you are just getting ready to reach for the bottle. The whole movement is already there, in the power of movement, before you make it. That is why you don't have to grope around: he already has it all figured out, exactly where his hand is going to go and where it is going to end up, and it is going to grab the bottle. And just before he moves, somebody else grabs the bottle.

You can learn two things from this. Nothing happened: it did not come out to the outside; it stayed a *hiyuli*. It never came out, and yet it was completely prepared to do it. (A student: "It's like he was about to do it." "Yeah, it was all prepared in there.") And had nobody else grabbed it and he grabbed it, that preparation is connected to the outside, to the actual grabbing; it is not that something else happened. In other words, the absence he speaks of is not necessarily an absence. That is just how you see it, from the absence and the hindrance.

phrases.he: אבל ההכנה בעצמה כבר בשלימותה,
phrases.en: But the preparation itself is already complete,

phrases.he: ולא חסר רק לבא בהתגלות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and all that is missing is to come into revelation in actual deed;

phrases.he: דהיינו שכבר שיער היטב בעצמו בדרך פרט
phrases.en: that is, he has already estimated well in himself, in particular,

phrases.he: לאותו דבר שבא לפועל ממש
phrases.en: for that thing which comes into actual deed,

phrases.he: והיינו שיער בעצמו בכח מה שצריך להביא בפועל
phrases.en: that is, he estimated in himself, in potential, what has to be brought into deed.

blocks.text: **the preparation itself is already complete**; **all that is missing is to come into revelation in actual deed**. He has already estimated in himself, in particular, the thing that comes into actual deed: like to grab the bottle.

sections.title: The examples, and the contraction that brings the spiritual into the physical
sections.summary: The power of movement, the spirit of life and the power of growth each have the three levels, and all three are joined even to the deed: one grabs the bottle with the *yechida* itself. Yet the deed is physical, a different thing, and getting there needs a *tzimtzum*; without it a man freezes, or cannot get a word out.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא הנזכר לעיל בכח התנועה
phrases.en: As in the example mentioned above, of the power of movement

phrases.he: כשעתידה לצאת בגלוי בדבר פרט
phrases.en: when it is about to come out into the open, in a particular thing.

blocks.text: **the power of movement when it is about to come out**, like to grab a bottle. That means that even if he did make this movement, it is connected to this third level.

blocks.title: "When you're finished, pass the bottle over"
blocks.text: Now, what happens when the other guy grabbed the bottle and the power of movement did not come into action? What does he do? He says to the guy, "When you're finished, pass the bottle over." Notice that the same power of movement, which in the essence of the soul was just a desire to grab the bottle, really the desire to get himself a drink of vodka, turned into the power of speech. And it is not a separate thing; it is *mamash* the same thing. Even in *Kadmon* it is *mamash* one, but there you can already say it is a unification of powers that are unified like one. The power of movement turned into the power of speech, and the exact same motivation that had him all prepared to grab the bottle turned into the motivation to tell the guy to pass it when he is finished.

So you learn both of these things from it. When it does not happen, you see that it is all prepared, and yet it is not necessary that it happen; and even when it does happen, the *hiyuli* is still just a *hiyuli*. And second, you see that one power can turn into another power.

phrases.he: וכמו התפשטות החיות להחיות לגוף כשמוכן לצאת
phrases.en: And like the spreading of life to enliven the body, when it is ready to come out,

phrases.he: שכלולים שם ביחוד כללי כל החיות פרטיי'
phrases.en: where all the particular powers of life are included there in a general unity.

phrases.he: ואח"כ הוא מה ששיער והכין כבר בכח התנועה איך להניע דרך פרט
phrases.en: And after that is what he has already estimated and prepared in the power of movement, how to move in a particular way.

phrases.he: וכן מה ששיער התגלות התפשטות רוח החיים,
phrases.en: So too when he estimates the revelation of the spreading of the spirit of life,

phrases.he: והוכן בו מה שעתיד להחיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and what it will actually enliven is already prepared in it.

blocks.title: "Liven up, we got a big job ahead of us"
blocks.text: When he estimates how much revelation of the spirit of life there is going to be, what he is going to enliven in actual deed is already included: for instance when he is psyching himself up to run or something like that, and he is going to need an extra influx of the spirit of life. When you are going to do a real heavy action, you have to get some extra life, like they tell you, "Wake up, liven up"; like they tell the soldiers, "Liven up, we got a big job ahead of us."

phrases.he: וכמו כן דמיון כח הצומח
phrases.en: And so too the comparison of the power of growth

phrases.he: כשמוכן להצמיח בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: when it is ready to make [a plant] actually grow:

phrases.he: שיש בזה גם כן ענין ג' מדריגות הללו
phrases.en: it too has these three levels.

blocks.text: The power of growth in the ground, when it is *mamash* already connected to a tree and ready actually to give the tree the power to grow, **it too has these three levels**. Each of these powers has these three levels, and they are all connected even to the actual deed. The deed is connected not just to *Kadmon*: *Kadmon* is connected to *Echad*, and *Echad* to *Yachid*.

That means when he is actually grabbing for the bottle, really he is grabbing it with *Yachid*, with the essence of the *yechida*. It goes through the two conduits, *Echad* and *Kadmon*: there has to be a point where the powers come out and it is not just the essence of the *yechida*, since they come out in particular; and then a point where they come out not just in general but for this particular action, where the action is estimated.

phrases.he: והכל הוא טרם שבא הדבר עדיין בפועל ממש
phrases.en: And all this is before the thing has actually come into deed,

phrases.he: כמו התנועה קודם שבאה בגשם הנפעל
phrases.en: like the movement before it comes into the physical thing that is moved,

phrases.he: או החיות הרוחני קודם שבא בגשם הגוף
phrases.en: or the spiritual life before it comes into the physical body,

phrases.he: ששם משתנה ממהות רוחנית למהות גשם,
phrases.en: where it changes from a spiritual being into a physical being,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת תנועה גשמיות
phrases.en: which is physical movement

phrases.he: והחיות גשמיות
phrases.en: and physical life;

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא בגשם הצמיחה כו'
phrases.en: and the like in the physical plant.

blocks.text: We are not talking about the actual coming out into the deed. Even when it is coming out into the deed, this is the inner power, which does not come into the deed.

Where it actually comes into an actual movement, the movement is not the thing of the soul anymore. It is a physical movement; and the life is physical too. And so **in the physical plant**, the actual plant: it is not the power of growth at all. It is a different thing; it is a plant, like a piece of wood.

phrases.he: שצריך לזה בחינת צמצום וכיווץ בגלוי זה הרוחני בתחלה,
phrases.en: for which a *tzimtzum* and a contraction of this spiritual revelation is needed first,

phrases.he: כדי שיבוא מכלל רוחניות לגשמיות
phrases.en: so that it may come from the realm of the spiritual to the physical

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר באות הי''ב):
phrases.en: (as will be explained in section 12).

blocks.title: Costello and the Wolf Man
blocks.text: **a *tzimtzum* and a contraction … is needed first**. The example: "Did you ever see Abbott and Costello and the Wolf Man?" (They work out who is who: Abbott is the tall one, the straight man, Costello the short one.) Costello is standing there, Abbott is standing there, and the Wolf Man is standing behind Abbott, and Costello goes [he acts out the sputtering]. Why is he doing that? Because he is so panicked by seeing the Wolf Man that he cannot *metzamtzem* (contract) his speech into the particular letters. He wants to say the whole speech as it is inside him, at one shot. And since he cannot make a *tzimtzum*, he cannot make the particular thing.

blocks.title: Frozen before a Tyrannosaurus Rex
blocks.text: The same thing happens if you are walking down the street and all of a sudden a Tyrannosaurus Rex looms up over you: people freeze. Why do they freeze? You should be running. They freeze because it is such a big shock that the whole power of movement is coming out at one shot, and he cannot make a *tzimtzum*, which way to go, into a particular movement. He is trying to make all the movements, to run all different ways at once, and since he cannot make the *tzimtzum*, he cannot run any way at all.

And this is in many, many things. Why, if you cannot make the *tzimtzum*? Because the spiritual power is infinite; it is not for a particular movement. And the power of speech is not for a particular thing, so if you cannot make the *tzimtzum*, and you have to make it all the way down to the letters, nothing comes out.
That is also why people stutter: they are trying to put the whole thought into the speech at one shot. And what you have to teach them is how to slow down and make a *tzimtzum*.

sensitivity.reason: Gives a cause of stuttering and a way to treat it ("teach them how to slow down"), which a reader might act on.
sensitivity.publishable: That is also why a person can stumble over his words: he is trying to put the whole thought into speech at one shot, without the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: So to come from the spiritual to the physical you have to make a *tzimtzum*, **as will be explained** with G-d's help in chapter 12.

When the tape goes on he sums up the chapter. In some places the *Or Ein Sof* is said to have nothing there: "not in the count of ten *sefiros*", "not of any of these attributes at all" and the like. In other places it says things like "He engraved an engraving in the *tehiru ila'a*", which means letters, and "the simple will", and "at the head of the King's authority". And it says "wise, but not with a known wisdom", which means there is a *chachma* there. So what's the story? It says there are *sefiros* there and it says there are no *sefiros* there.

What he explains is that when we say there are no *sefiros* there, it does not mean they are lacking there. It means it is totally higher than the matter of *sefiros* altogether, to the point that you cannot say there is an actual *chachma* there, any more than you can say there is a will for shoes in a *chesed*. But on the other hand you cannot take them out of there. If you say there is no *chachma*, you are actually insulting the *Aibershter*. What do you mean, He has no *chachma* at all? So the *Aibershter* is stupid? That is what "no *chachma*" means; it is an insult. If you separate any one of the *sefiros* out of there, you are a *kofer b'ikar* (one who denies the essence), *mamash* a *kofer* in the *Aibershter*.

blocks.title: "I don't do shoes"
blocks.text: It is like the *chesed* we spoke of. The guy will help you out with certain things, but with others he says, "Well, I don't do shoes." If you don't do shoes, and this poor guy is walking around with bleeding feet, it means you don't have *chesed*, period. "Yeah, but I do all these other things. I have a fund for coats, and I have a fund for feeding people. I just won't do shoes." Well, here is a guy standing right in front of you with his feet bleeding, and you won't do shoes: you *mamash* don't have *chesed*. You are not an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness). "I don't care what else you do." And you say, what do you mean, a *chesed* is not made up of a *chesed* for shoes? Yes, it is not; but on the other hand, if you take out this one piece of it, you took out the whole thing.

So the same thing: even though there are no ten *sefiros* up there, if you take out one *sefira*, or even a *sefira* of a *sefira*, like *netzach* of *netzach* of *tiferes*, and say "I believe there are all these things up there except for *netzach* of *tiferes*", you are totally a *kofer* in the essence. And the basic point of the whole matter: "if not, where would these particulars come from?" That is basically the whole thing there, and that is what we learned until now.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the introduction insist that *hisbonenus* is *iyun* and not meditation, and why must it be done in particulars?
Why is even the name *Yachid* not quite right for the first level?
What does "wise, but not with a known wisdom" mean, and why may one not simply say there is no *chachma* there?
How do the *schnorrers* know a man will help them, and how do they know he will give pants he never gave anyone?
Why is a foundation that gives only shoes no longer a *chesed*, and what does that teach about taking one *sefira* out of the Essence?
What does the bottle of vodka at a *farbrengen* show about *Kadmon*, and what happens when someone else grabs it first?
